title: Developer Task Delegation to LLMs and the Trust Factor: A Mixed Methods Study
title_zh: 开发者向LLM委派任务与信任因素：一项混合方法研究

paragraphs.en: With the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs), software developers are presented with a powerful new approach: delegating software development tasks to LLMs. Existing studies have explored task delegation for a subset of tasks and factors. Critically, what tasks developers delegate to LLMs, to what extent, and why they delegate them, is not yet well understood. We explore these questions through 22 interviews and a survey with 160 software practitioners. Developers reported employing four modes of task delegation to LLMs: full delegation, partial delegation, self-delegation, and task avoidance. Drawing on our qualitative findings, we discuss the rationales behind these choices and explore how task difficulty, task risk, developer motivation, and trust appear to be associated with software development task delegation to LLMs. Our statistical analysis reveals that trust is a significant factor associated with task delegation to LLMs. Finally, we share actionable implications for human-AI collaboration in software research, and for software practitioners to make the most of their newly found powers of delegation.
paragraphs.zh: 随着大语言模型（LLMs）的兴起，软件开发者迎来了一种强大的新方法：将软件开发任务委托给 LLMs。 已有研究针对部分任务子集和相关因素探索了任务委托。 关键在于，开发者将哪些任务委托给 LLMs、委托到何种程度，以及为何委托，目前尚不清晰。 我们通过对 22 位受访者的访谈和针对 160 名软件从业者的调查来探索这些问题。 开发者报告了向 LLMs 委托任务的四种模式：完全委托、部分委托、自我委托和任务回避。 基于我们的定性研究结果，我们讨论了这些选择背后的理由，并探讨任务难度、任务风险、开发者动机和信任似乎如何与向 LLMs 委托软件开发任务相关联。 我们的统计分析表明，信任是与向 LLMs 委托任务相关联的一个显著因素。 最后，我们为软件研究中的人机协作提供了可操作的建议，并帮助软件从业者充分利用其新获得的委托能力。

paragraphs.en: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has equipped software developers with an unprecedented ability to delegate development tasks to coding agents [ 1 ] . The 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey reported that 78.5% of developers are now using AI tools in their development process [ 2 ] . The 2025 DORA report [ 3 ] found that developers frequently rely on AI for tasks such as writing new code, modifying existing code, creating test cases, and explaining concepts. Similar trends are also quoted in industry practice. For example, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella reported that “up to 30% of the company’s code was written by AI” [ 4 ] . However, many recent incidents, such as Replit-agent failure [ 5 , 6 ] , highlight the risks associated with excessive delegation to autonomous systems without adequate safeguards. In that case, the agent reportedly made “unauthorised changes to live infrastructure, wiping out data for more than 1200 executives and over 1,190 companies” . These incidents underscore the importance of maintaining appropriate human oversight and control when integrating AI into software development workflows. There are also concerns that delegating too many tasks to LLM agents “dumbs-down” human software developers and reduces their ability to review and correct LLM-made errors [ 7 , 8 ] .

paragraphs.en: While developers are pushing the limits of delegating tasks to LLMs in practice, with mixed consequences, research is beginning to explore the advantages and risks of using LLMs and the different ways in which they are being used for software development tasks. For example, LLMs’ automation capabilities are gaining traction as a promising solution to assist developers by handling tedious and repetitive tasks [ 9 , 10 , 11 ] , such as reading documentation and web searches [ 12 ] . In some cases, automation has been found to enable developers to shift their focus to other activities that demand their expertise and creativity [ 13 , 14 ] . Automation of some tasks, such as code generation and information retrieval, has been found to reduce developer effort [ 15 ] . Hassan et al. [ 16 ] proposed Software Engineering (SE) 3.0, an AI-native approach for development between human developers and AI teammates. However, drawbacks of adopting LLMs, such as fragmenting developers’ mental model of the codebase and hindering their SE skills are also emerging [ 15 ] .

paragraphs.en: To answer our RQs, we conducted a mixed-methods study involving semi-structured interviews with 22 software practitioners, followed by a survey focused on software development tasks with 160 software practitioners. From this study, we identified four developer task delegation to LLMs modes: full delegation, partial delegation, self-delegation, and task avoidance grounded in empirical evidence. Full delegation involves minimal developer intervention in LLMs’ actions, only reviewing LLMs’ final output. Partial delegation requires active, close management of LLMs’ actions, demanding higher developer engagement. Self-delegation occurs when developers bypass LLMs entirely, relying instead on traditional resources like Google search or Stack Overflow. Task avoidance occurs when developers choose to completely evade a task, despite having access to LLM assistance. We identified that task difficulty , task risk , developer motivation , and developer trust towards LLMs are key factors shaping task delegation. From our statistical analysis, we found evidence that developer trust towards LLMs is a significant factor associated with full or partial task delegation.

paragraphs.en: Recent studies explore how LLMs influence software practitioners’ task delegation decisions (e.g., [ 17 , 20 , 18 ] ) and are summarised in section IV . To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to present four modes of developer task delegation to LLMs. These modes were identified through the analysis of exploratory interviews and subsequently complemented by a survey. In this paper, we also investigate the socio-technical factors behind these delegation decisions, examining how task difficulty, task risk, developer motivation, and trust in LLMs are associated with the mode of task delegation.
paragraphs.zh: 近期研究探讨了 LLM 如何影响软件从业者的任务委派决策（例如 [17, 20, 18]），并在第 IV 节中进行了总结。 据我们所知，这是首个提出开发者向 LLM 委派任务的四种模式的研究。 这些模式是通过对探索性访谈的分析识别出来的，随后通过一项调查加以补充。 在本文中，我们还研究了这些委派决策背后的社会技术因素，考察任务难度、任务风险、开发者动机以及对 LLM 的信任与任务委派模式之间的关联。

paragraphs.en: To do this, we applied a mixed methods research approach using an exploratory sequential design [ 22 ] . We first explored the use of LLMs in software development through qualitative semi-structured interviews. We then followed these interviews with practitioner mixed-data survey, with quantitative data from the closed-ended questions and qualitative data from the open-ended questions. Figure 1 provides an overview of our study methodology. The supplementary material [ 23 ] includes the pre-interview questionnaire, the interview guide, the survey questions, examples of qualitative data analysis, and quantitative data analysis scripts, in line with the requirements of the ethical research approval gained for the study. In the following, we describe the two sequential phases of the study. The interviews helped to address RQ1, while the hypotheses resulting from the interviews and the survey results helped to address some of RQ1 and all of RQ2.

paragraphs.en: We recruited software developers with experience in using LLMs for software development from LinkedIn, X (formerly Twitter), personal connections, and through word-of-mouth snowballing. We use the term software developer “as an umbrella term in the SE context” , encompassing a range of roles including but not limited to web development and requirements engineering [ 24 ] . Each interviewee filled a 10-minute pre-interview questionnaire and participated in a semi-structured interview. The pre-interview questionnaire collected demographics, LLM experience, and Attitudes towards Artificial Intelligence (ATAI scale) [ 25 ] . ATAI scale involves the following five eleven-point scale questions: (1) I fear artificial intelligence ; (2) I trust AI ; (3) AI will destroy humankind; (4) AI will benefit humankind ; and (5) AI will cause many job losses . It was used to understand participants’ attitudes towards AI in general, not limited to LLMs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过 LinkedIn、X（原 Twitter）、个人关系以及口碑滚雪球式推荐，招募了具有使用大语言模型（LLM）进行软件开发经验的软件开发者。 我们将「软件开发者」用作“软件工程语境下的一个总括性术语”，涵盖包括但不限于网页开发和需求工程在内的一系列角色 [ 24 ] 。 每位受访者填写了一份10分钟的访谈前问卷，并参加了半结构化访谈。 访谈前问卷收集了人口统计学信息、LLM使用经验以及人工智能态度（ATAI量表）[ 25 ] 。 ATAI量表包含以下五个十一分制问题：(1) 我害怕人工智能；(2) 我信任AI；(3) AI将毁灭人类；(4) AI将造福人类；(5) AI将导致大量失业。 该量表用于了解参与者对人工智能的整体态度，而不限于LLM。

paragraphs.en: Interviews were then conducted by the first author over three rounds between October (2024) and September (2025) and lasted between 34 to 58 minutes. Although not mentioned in the study advertisement to avoid unscrupulous interviewees, we provided a (currency and amount withheld for anonymous review) gift voucher to each interview participant after the interview to express our gratitude for their commitment. Our semi-structured interview questions explored participants’ experiences, perceptions of adopting LLMs in software development, factors associated with their adoption, and their attitudes regarding task delegation to LLMs. We conducted two pilot interviews with experienced software practitioners to evaluate the interview questions and structure, which resulted in minor refinements. We excluded the data from these pilot interviews from the final interview pool, as they did not have experience using LLMs for software development.

paragraphs.en: We used socio-technical grounded theory for data analysis (STGT4DA) [ 26 ] to analyse the qualitative data from the semi-structured interviews to derive layered and nuanced findings, as has been applied in similar contexts [ 27 , 28 , 29 ] . The first author conducted the data analysis, applying open coding, constant comparison (see Figure 2 ), and memoing. Instead of applying quantitative metrics such as inter-rater/coder reliability, which are widely considered epistemologically incompatible with the inductive qualitative data analysis techniques [ 26 , 30 , 31 , 32 ] , we focused on collaborative alignment [ 26 ] : the co-authors reviewed the emerging codes and concepts regularly throughout the process, and we also conducted dedicated coding workshops to align our initial coding principles and critically review the concepts, categories, and socio-technical findings.
paragraphs.zh: 我们采用社会技术扎根理论数据分析方法（STGT4DA）[ 26 ] 对半结构化访谈的定性数据进行分析，以得出分层且细致入微的发现，该方法已在类似情境中得到应用 [ 27 , 28 , 29 ] 。 第一作者进行了数据分析，应用了开放式编码、持续比较（见图 2 ）和备忘录撰写。 我们没有采用评分者/编码者间信度等定量指标——这些指标被普遍认为在认识论上与归纳式定性数据分析技术不相容 [ 26 , 30 , 31 , 32 ] ——而是聚焦于协作对齐 [ 26 ] ：共同作者在整个过程中定期审阅不断涌现的编码与概念，我们还开展了专门的编码研讨会，以对齐我们最初的编码原则，并对概念、类别以及社会技术发现进行批判性审阅。

paragraphs.en: To better understand how our proposed task delegation modes manifest across a broader population and to test our hypotheses, we conducted an anonymous 15-minute survey with software practitioners. Our survey followed Kitchenham and Pfleeger’s guidelines [ 33 ] , combining both open and closed ended questions, including demographics, LLM experience, ATAI scale, task delegation modes, and Task Delegability to AI framework (TDAI). Aligned with our emerging factors from the interview analysis, we employed a slightly modified version of the TDAI framework [ 34 , 35 ] that includes LLMs and GenAI in the questions to assess our hypotheses regarding difficulty , risk , motivation , and trust . TDAI allowed us to measure our emerging factors through the survey, comprehending fourteen questions measured using a five-point Likert framework. We share the survey questions in the supplementary package [ 23 ] . Through five pilots, we narrowed down the long list of SE tasks developers use LLMs documented by Hou et al. [ 9 ] to the following 17 coding-related tasks to fit our short survey format: code generation, code completion, code comment generation, code representation, API document smells, API recommendation, API document augment, API entity and relation extraction, type inference, code summarisation, code search, code understanding, code translation, method name generation, control flow graph generation, agile story point estimation , and data analysis . We decided to include the last two pilot survey responses into the survey dataset since the core questions did not change significantly after that.

paragraphs.en: We initially distributed our Qualtrics survey via LinkedIn and across our personal networks in December (2025). Similar to the interview participants, the survey participants were required to have experience of using LLM tools for software development tasks. After receiving only one response over almost one month, we then distributed the survey via Prolific , an online recruitment platform [ 36 ] . To ensure the quality of the responses, we employed attention checks [ 37 ] and authentication checks to filter AI-generated responses. The survey was administered in January (2026) and then in May (2026). From the 187 responses collected via Prolific, our manual review resulted in 155 (82.8%) accepted survey submissions, including only participants reporting having experience using LLMs for SE tasks. Each Prolific survey participant was rewarded (currency and amount withheld for anonymous review) after completing the survey. In total, we collected 160 survey responses, including 155 Prolific responses, three responses from LinkedIn, and two from the pilot survey.

paragraphs.en: To analyse the survey’s quantitative data, we calculated descriptive statistics for each closed-ended survey item to identify overall response patterns and trends. We then performed statistical analysis to examine whether difficulty , risk , motivation , and trust are positively or negatively associated with task delegation to LLMs. Before conducting our statistical analysis, we assessed the psychometric properties of the TDAI framework through multilevel coefficient omega ( ω \omega ), which accounts for the nested structure of our data (repeated task ratings within participants), and variance inflation factor (VIF). Between-person reliability was strong across all subscales ( ω b ​ e ​ t ​ w ​ e ​ e ​ n \omega_{between} =0.744–0.947). Within-person reliability was acceptable for motivation ( ω w ​ i ​ t ​ h ​ i ​ n \omega_{within} =0.785) and risk ( ω w ​ i ​ t ​ h ​ i ​ n \omega_{within} =0.628), but modest for difficulty ( ω w ​ i ​ t ​ h ​ i ​ n \omega_{within} =0.544) and trust ( ω w ​ i ​ t ​ h ​ i ​ n \omega_{within} =0.512). Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC=0.476–0.692) further confirmed that a substantial proportion of variance in all subscales reflected stable individual differences rather than task-specific responses. VIF values ranged 1.02–1.32 at the within-person level and 1.14–1.45 at the between-person level. Pairwise correlations did not exceed 0.47 at either level.

paragraphs.en: We fitted a sequential binary mixed-effects logistic regression model [ 38 ] by decomposing the ordinal three task delegation modes outcome (i.e., full delegation , partial delegation , and self-delegation ) with sufficient data into two distinct, nested binary transitions. Task avoidance was excluded from the regression model because of it is marginally selected in practice, having a small sample size (n=21). A standard ordinal logistic regression model would treat the outcome as a single linear progression and impose the proportional odds assumption, requiring each factor to have the same effect at every step of the scale. Preliminary testing showed that this assumption was violated, meaning that the relationship between the factors and task delegation mode changes depending on which transition is being modelled. Sequential binary logistic regression analysis addresses this issue by explicitly decomposing the ordinal outcome into two binary decisions that reflect the natural decision process underlying the data. paragraphs.en: Figure 3 summarises the SE tasks, task delegation modes, and reasons identified in the interviews. Our qualitative analysis reveals that participants’ willingness to delegate tasks to LLMs is primary governed by opportunities for time savings, particularly for low-stakes tasks, and by situations in which they experience low personal motivation to perform the work themselves. paragraphs.en: Figure 4 illustrates how participants distribute their task delegation modes (full delegation, partial delegation, self-delegation, task avoidance) across 17 distinct SE tasks. Across almost all tasks, partial delegation to LLMs (n=516) emerged as the dominant task delegation mode, indicating that developers predominantly use LLMs as collaborative tools rather than autonomous agents. While full delegation (n=209) was observed for every task, it remained uncommon compared to partial delegation, even for tasks strongly associated with generative AI, such as code generation (n=15). In total, the self-delegation mode (n=132) was the third most common delegation mode, occurring less frequently than both partial delegation and full delegation across many tasks. In contrast, the task avoidance mode was consistently the least common across tasks, indicating that participants rarely chose to forgo a task despite having access to LLM support. This pattern suggests that developers are generally willing to leverage LLM assistance to complete tasks rather than performing them entirely on their own, while outright task avoidance remains uncommon. However, we did not collect data on how frequently participants performed each task daily. Hence, differences in delegation patterns should be interpreted cautiously as they may reflect not only task characteristics but also variation in participants’ exposure to or experience with particular tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 图 4 展示了参与者在 17 个不同的软件工程（SE）任务上如何分配其任务委托模式（完全委托、部分委托、自我委托、任务回避）。 在几乎所有任务中，向大语言模型（LLM）的部分委托（n=516）都成为占主导地位的任务委托模式，这表明开发者主要将 LLM 用作协作工具，而非自主的智能体。 尽管每个任务都观察到了完全委托（n=209），但与部分委托相比它仍然少见，即使对于与生成式人工智能强相关的任务（如代码生成，n=15）也是如此。 总体而言，自我委托模式（n=132）是第三常见的委托模式，在许多任务中其出现频率低于部分委托和完全委托。 相比之下，任务回避模式在各项任务中始终最为少见，这表明尽管可以使用 LLM 支持，参与者很少选择放弃任务。 这一模式表明，开发者通常愿意借助 LLM 的辅助来完成任务，而不是完全靠自己完成，而彻底的任务回避仍然少见。 然而，我们并未收集关于参与者每天执行每个任务频率的数据。 因此，对委托模式差异的解读应当谨慎，因为这些差异可能不仅反映了任务特征，还反映了参与者接触特定任务或在其中积累经验的程度差异。

paragraphs.en: We found interview participants partially [3] or fully delegating the following SE tasks to LLMs: system design, diagram generation, code generation, code translation, test generation, document generation, and code review. Their reasons for delegation are mainly that LLMs can free developers’ time from low-stakes, repetitive or tedious tasks, and developers’ self-admitted laziness. IP16 and IP13 express how they become dependent on LLMs – e.g., “I have become lazy [to write] even if [it is just a] small one line, I can also rely on the LLMs.” (IP16, R&D Software Engineer). IP10 mentions trusting in LLMs for minor and low-risk tasks, which will not result in much damage, e.g., “If I am going to do some cosmetic changes, for example, […] I just want to change how the page looks without actually affecting the logic. I think the LLMs will be a pretty safe bet to do because I’m not risking [inserting] bugs on the business logic” (IP10, Software Engineer).
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现访谈参与者将以下软件工程（SE）任务部分 [3] 或完全委托给大语言模型（LLM）：系统设计、图表生成、代码生成、代码翻译、测试生成、文档生成和代码审查。 他们委托的原因主要是大语言模型可以让开发者从低风险、重复或繁琐的任务中解放时间，以及开发者自己承认的懒惰。 IP16 和 IP13 表达了他们如何变得依赖大语言模型——例如，“即使只是小小的一行代码，我也变得懒得写，反正可以依赖大语言模型。”（IP16，研发软件工程师）。 IP10 提到在次要的低风险任务上信任大语言模型，因为这类任务不会造成太大损失，例如，“如果我要做一些外观上的修改，比如……我只是想改变页面的外观，而实际上不影响逻辑。 我认为大语言模型是相当安全的选择，因为我不会冒着在业务逻辑中 [插入] 缺陷的风险”（IP10，软件工程师）。

paragraphs.en: System Design & Diagram Generation. Two interview participants reported delegating system design or diagram generation to LLMs. IP12 collected the requirements and asked ChatGPT to generate the system design, providing the company context, e.g.: [3] “I let ChatGPT know: ‘These are the requirements, these are the stories that I collected from each person […] Can you give me a good solution for this? And these are the existing systems that you can use […] [According to ChatGPT,] this is just an authentication/authorisation system […] Then I was like: ‘Yeah, this is good”’ (IP12, Software Engineer). IP10 partially delegates diagram generation to LLMs: [3] “If I have described an architecture, [I can say to the LLMs:] ‘Now, please create the diagram for this architecture’. [Then, the LLMs] it creates the mermaid diagram, so it can easily be visualised how this architecture works”’ (IP10, Software Engineer). Related to diagram generation, Figure 4 shows that 82% of survey participants delegate code representation to LLMs, with 53% delegating fully and 29% partially.

paragraphs.en: Code Generation. Five interview participants reported delegating code generation to LLMs. Figure 4 shows that 70% of survey participants partially delegate code generation to LLMs, and only 11% fully delegate. Although IP20 still enjoys coding, they decide to delegate tedious or repetitive coding to LLMs: [3] “I still find sometimes writing code myself, it’s way better than integrating with an LLM. And I only really use an LLM if the task that I’m about to do is really tedious and repetitive” (IP20, Software Engineer). Regarding tedious coding tasks, IP4 mentions the coding task of building a JSONBean: “If you’ve ever done a query in JSONBean, the query gets very ugly. You write it about fifteen times until you get the syntax right. Then I said [to LLM]: ‘I have a JSON like this that has the information that’s there, I created a SQL query for myself that I’m going to throw into the database, and it’s going to return what I want’. That’s it, the LLM generated it quickly and gave it to me.” (IP4, Software Developer).

paragraphs.en: Our analysis of survey open-ended responses reveals that level of control, ownership and accountability, developer effort, developer mental model, and requirements play a role in developers’ minds when comparing full delegation and partial delegation. For instance, developers need to closely manage the models’ actions in partial delegation, e.g.: “In partial delegation, there is continuous human oversight and the LLM is responsible for only specific tasks” (SP123, Software Engineer). On the other hand, minimal human input is required in full delegation, e.g.: “Full delegation means handling off an entire task to the LLM with minimal human involvement” (SP118, Software Engineer). In summary, participants differ partial delegation from full delegation in the level of human engagement, but both require human review.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对问卷开放式回答的分析表明，在比较完全委托与部分委托时，控制程度、所有权与问责、开发者投入、开发者心智模型以及需求等因素都在开发者的考量之中。 例如，在部分委托中，开发者需要密切管理模型的行为，例如：“在部分委托中，存在持续的人类监督，LLM 只负责特定任务”（SP123，软件工程师）。 另一方面，完全委托只需要极少的人类输入，例如：“完全委托意味着将整个任务交给 LLM，人类参与极少”（SP118，软件工程师）。 总而言之，参与者在人类参与程度上区分部分委托与完全委托，但两者都需要人类审查。

paragraphs.en: Our findings indicate that certain developers deliberately resist AI assistance for specific tasks despite model availability. For instance, IP11 explicitly noted that they never write documentation even when they had access to LLMs. This stance aligns with our broader survey analysis, which identified a subset of participants who would prefer to avoid LLMs even when actively employing them for other development tasks. These tasks, illustrated in Figure 4 , include code generation (n=4), code understanding (n=4), code completion (n=3), and data analysis (n=2). Respondents attributed this systematic aversion to several critical socio-technical barriers: perceived LLM limitations (e.g., the introduction of security vulnerabilities), strict requirements for handling sensitive information, the indispensable need for human review and legal accountability, a lack of developer expertise, a lack of trust in LLMs, specific task characteristics, and a fundamental desire to maintain human control over the codebase.

paragraphs.en: Figure 5 captures the interplay between these four emerging factors towards LLM task delegation. Each factor is measured on a 0–4 scale, and the resulting task delegation level is measured on a 0–3 scale across 17 coding-related tasks. paragraphs.en: Through a survey with 188 software engineers, Lambiase et al. [ 17 ] investigated the relationship between individual attributes related to technology adoption and LLM adoption for five specific SE tasks: manipulating artifacts, generating alternative versions of an artifact, retrieving information from external sources, supporting decisions through recommendations and contextual insights, and training in theoretical or practical knowledge of software concepts. They found that LLM adoption for SE might not be uniform across different tasks and argued that LLM adoption is a “domain-specific phenomenon rather than a broadly generalizable trend” .

paragraphs.en: Sergeyuk et al. [ 18 ] conducted a survey with 481 software developers to understand how software developers are using AI assistants, which tasks they are not using AI for, and what improvements are necessary in these assistants. They focused on five SE activities: implementing new features, writing tests, bug triaging, refactoring, and writing natural-language artifacts. Their findings indicate that: 84.2% of the survey respondents occasionally or regularly used AI assistants; implementing new features was the most common activity; and code generation and code summarisation were the most common tasks. They also found that writing tests in general and generating data and resources for tests were less enjoyable tasks, which developers preferred to delegate to AI tools. They classified developers’ motivations for not using LLMs into 20 themes. The most recurrent themes were the lack of need for AI assistance, AI-generated output being inaccurate, users’ lack of trust and the desire to feel in control, and limitations of AI assistants in understanding context. Our findings align with Sergeyuk [ 18 ] regarding the relationship between perceived task difficulty and willingness to delegate. Their correlation analysis across five SE tasks similarly demonstrated a lack of statistical significance. However, our findings arise from evaluating these dynamics across a larger pool of SE tasks and based on tasks that our participants reported having experience in using LLMs.

paragraphs.en: Choudhuri et al. [ 20 ] explored how software developers’ evaluations of their tasks shape their preference for where, why, and how AI should support their workflows. They conducted a survey with 840 Microsoft developers using perceived task significance ( value ), level of alignment with developers’ interests and expertise ( identity ), perceived responsibility and blame ( accountability ), and task effort ( demands ) as study metrics. They used their synthesised literature-grounded taxonomy of SE tasks. They also employed Microsoft’s Responsible AI framework [ 39 ] to assess developers’ Responsible AI priorities. Their findings indicate that task value, accountability, and demands positively influence AI openness and use, while developers’ interests and expertise (identity) may lead to lower public support for AI, even as their usage remains higher. They also observed great receptivity from junior, AI-experienced, risk-tolerant, and technophilic developers. Our results reinforce those of Choudhuri et al. [ 40 ] , who found that trust is directly associated with actual LLM usage among software developers at Microsoft and GitHub. Our study expands on their work by demonstrating that trust is vital not just for adoption, but specifically for navigating both the initial adoption and subsequent autonomy stage.
paragraphs.zh: Choudhuri 等人 [ 20 ] 探讨了软件开发者对其任务的评估如何影响他们对 AI 应在何处、为何以及如何支持其工作流程的偏好。 他们对 840 名 Microsoft 开发者进行了调查，采用感知任务重要性（value）、与开发者兴趣和专业知识的契合程度（identity）、感知的责任与归咎（accountability）以及任务投入（demands）作为研究指标。 他们使用了其综合文献构建的软件工程（SE）任务分类法。 他们还采用了 Microsoft 的负责任 AI 框架 [ 39 ] 来评估开发者在负责任 AI 方面的优先事项。 他们的研究结果表明，任务价值、问责性和投入正向影响对 AI 的开放态度和使用，而开发者的兴趣和专业知识（identity）可能导致对 AI 的公开支持度较低，即便其使用率仍然较高。 他们还观察到初级开发者、有 AI 经验的开发者、风险容忍型开发者以及技术爱好者型开发者表现出极高的接受度。 我们的结果印证了 Choudhuri 等人 [ 40 ] 的发现，即信任与 Microsoft 和 GitHub 软件开发者对大语言模型（LLM）的实际使用直接相关。 我们的研究扩展了他们的工作，证明信任不仅对采纳至关重要，尤其对于 navigating 初始采纳和后续自主阶段的两个过程都至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Based on our findings and corroborating with related works, we suggest the following implications for software practitioners.
paragraphs.zh: 基于我们的发现并结合相关研究的印证，我们为软件从业者提出以下启示。

paragraphs.en: Do not expect developers to blindly delegate code generation to LLMs. Figure 4 shows that 70% of the participants partially delegate, 16% self-delegate, and only 11% fully delegate code generation . The level of trust plays a significant role in this decision. Figure 5 shows that code generation ranks as the least trusted task (scoring 2.66 out of 4). The potential bugs from AI-generated code seems to make developers distrust LLMs for code generation (Section III-B3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 不要期望开发者会盲目地将代码生成委托给LLM。 图4显示，70%的参与者部分委托，16%自行完成，只有11%完全委托代码生成。 信任程度在这一决策中起着重要作用。 图5显示，代码生成是信任度最低的任务（得分为4分中的2.66分）。 AI生成代码可能带来的缺陷似乎使开发者对LLM进行代码生成缺乏信任（第III-B3节）。

paragraphs.en: Developers select partial delegation for most tasks – reflecting a balanced control towards LLMs. Partial delegation is the most frequent task delegation mode across the analysed tasks. Our findings show that 60% of developers choose this mode even though it demands more engagement from the developer as compared to full delegation (see Figure 4 ). This prevalent choice reflects a deliberate effort by developers to keep the code under active human control rather than handing it over blindly to the model, an idea captured as a balanced control in the reliance-control framework [ 8 ] .

paragraphs.en: Team task risk alignment is necessary. Our findings show that developers perceive task risk varying according to different tasks (see Figure 5 ). The danger is that developers undermine crucial tasks. For instance, as highlighted in Section III-B3 , some developers may misclassify tests as a low-stakes task. In this scenario, the team should align on how much they are willing to delegate to LLMs, balancing productivity gains and reliability.

paragraphs.en: Trust is a significant factor associated with the level of task delegation to LLMs. Through our mixed methods study, we identified trust as a significant factor associated with task delegation (Table IV and Figure 5 ). Our study provides empirical evidence of the claim made in the Communications of the ACM opinion piece by Roychoudhury et al. that said “with the increased use of AI code generation […] the emphasis will be not only on programming at scale, but increasingly on programming with trust” [ 41 ] , and highlights the need to better understand and improve developer trust.

paragraphs.en: From delegation to automation – LLM-based tool developers should focus on features that improve developer trust. Since trust is a significant factor associated with partial or full dev-LLM task delegation, LLM-based software development tools need features that help improve developer trust. For example, with increased developer trust, tasks close to full delegation (Fig. 5 ) could progress toward automation, reaching what has been referred to as escape velocity in industry, described as “the shift from AI as a tool to AI as an autonomous collaborator” [ 42 ] . Hassan et al. [ 43 ] capture this notion in specialised domain autonomy (level 4) and general domain autonomy (level 5) of their hierarchical framework for AI in SE. Efforts such as Wang et al. [ 44 ] , who designed a dashboard to communicate aggregate GitHub Copilot usage, represent initial steps toward designing for trust in LLM tools.
paragraphs.zh: 从委托到自动化——基于LLM的工具开发者应聚焦于能提升开发者信任的功能。 由于信任是影响开发者向LLM部分或全部委托任务的重要因素，基于LLM的软件开发工具需要具备有助于提升开发者信任的功能。 例如，随着开发者信任的提升，接近完全委托（图5）的任务可以朝着自动化的方向发展，最终达到业界所说的“逃逸速度”，即“从将AI作为工具转变为将AI作为自主协作者”。 Hassan等人[43]在其提出的AI在软件工程中的分层框架中，以专用领域自治（第4级）和通用领域自治（第5级）体现了这一理念。 Wang等人的工作 [44]设计了一个仪表盘来展示GitHub Copilot的总体使用情况，代表了面向LLM工具信任设计的初步探索。

paragraphs.en: Based on our study, we share some implications for research and ideas for future work.
paragraphs.zh: 基于我们的研究，我们分享了一些对研究工作的启示以及未来工作的想法。

paragraphs.en: What other factors drive task delegation? Future research could investigate other socio-technical factors, such as application domain (e.g., safety critical domains such a healthcare vs entertainment domains such as gaming) and interaction modes (e.g., chat-mode, voice mode, agentic terminal, IDE based AI). A deeper dive into how trust is manifested, enabled, and inhibited in developer-LLM collaboration will also help. Khati et al. [ 45 ] found that developer trust is associated with many factors (e.g., accuracy, interpretability) in their systematic literature review. They also pointed out that LLM trustworthiness, not just trust, must be addressed.

paragraphs.en: Internal Validity & Credibility – assesses whether empirical evidence robustly supports the study findings. We acknowledge that selection bias is an inherent threat in our study, as participants voluntarily opted to join both the interviews and the survey. We mitigate this by selecting only software practitioners with experience using LLMs for software development. We also recognise that research bias may have occurred during our qualitative and quantitative analysis. To ensure credibility, the first author conducted data analysis pilots in both interview and survey data analysis and was supervised by qualitative and mixed research experts. The first author also consulted two expert statisticians for guidance on the most suitable statistical approach. We observed considerable variation in the number of responses across tasks. Because we did not measure how frequently participants performed each task daily (to avoid respondent attrition due to an over lengthy survey), some differences in delegation patterns may reflect differences in participants’ exposure to particular tasks rather than task characteristics alone.

paragraphs.en: Our mixed-methods study set out to understand how software developers delegate tasks to LLMs in real-world practice, to what extent, and why. We interviewed 22 practitioners and surveyed 160 practitioners. Based on the analysis, we identified four software task delegation modes: full delegation to LLMs, partial delegation to LLMs, self-delegation , and task avoidance . Understanding these four task delegation modes is critical for both software engineering research and practice. For software organizations, these modes provide a concrete vocabulary to audit delegation patterns and evaluate risk exposure. For the research community, this study opens new avenues for modeling the socio-technical factors governing human-AI collaboration.
paragraphs.zh: 我们采用混合方法研究，旨在了解软件开发者在真实实践中如何将任务委托给LLM、委托程度如何以及原因何在。 我们访谈了22名从业者，并调查了160名从业者。 基于分析，我们识别出四种软件任务委托模式：完全委托给LLM、部分委托给LLM、自我委托和任务回避。 理解这四种任务委托模式对软件工程研究与实践都至关重要。 对软件组织而言，这些模式提供了一套具体的词汇，可用于审计委托模式并评估风险敞口。 对研究界而言，本研究为建模人机协作中的社会技术因素开辟了新途径。

paragraphs.en: We also explored why developers delegate the tasks they do and identified how task difficulty , task risk , developer motivation , and developer trust towards LLMs are associated with task delegation. Our findings confirm that developer trust towards LLMs is a significant factor associated with task delegation. For software organisations aiming to move developer-AI interactions from basic AI assistance toward autonomous task delegation, building a balanced level of developer trust in LLMs’ capabilities is essential.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还探讨了开发者为何委托他们所委托的任务，并识别了任务难度、任务风险、开发者动机以及开发者对大语言模型的信任与任务委托之间的关联。 我们的研究结果证实，开发者对大语言模型的信任是与任务委托相关的一个重要因素。 对于那些希望将开发者与人工智能的互动从基础的人工智能辅助推向自主任务委托的软件组织而言，建立开发者对大语言模型能力的适度信任水平至关重要。

sents.zh: 对于那些希望将开发者与人工智能的互动从基础的人工智能辅助推向自主任务委托的软件组织而言，建立开发者对大语言模型能力的适度信任水平至关重要。
